candidates.original_title: Children's and adults' judgments of equitable resource distributions
candidates.description: 5-and 6-year-olds' and parents' sensitivity to proportion when evaluating niceness of givers in collaborative versus individual effort contexts
candidates.citation_sentence: Consistent with previous reports [24], we found that children often focused on absolute amount rather than proportion when evaluating givers who shared individually earned resources, unlike adults who always considered proportion.
candidates.notes: Study 3 replicates key findings from Studies 1 and 2 using identical methods for children and caregivers; authors state 'replicated key findings from Studies 1 and 2' in the abstract. candidates.original_title: Children's and adults' judgments of equitable resource distributions
candidates.description: In a Giving Game, adults judge givers who provide a greater proportion of their available resources as nicer, whereas young children favor givers who provide a greater absolute amount.
candidates.citation_sentence: In Study 1, we tested 5-year-olds' sensitivity to proportion when assessing the "niceness" of givers in order to replicate [24].
candidates.notes: The full-text rendition represents the author-year citation as reference marker [24]; the cited original is McCrink, Bloom, and Santos (2010).
